thread.title: What the U.S. stock market does next may come down to this one decision

author: morningstar.com
title: What the U.S. stock market does next may come down to this one decision
text:
By Nigam Arora
The replacement for economic adviser Gary Cohn is crucial for investors
What the U.S. stock market does next may come down to one decision by President Trump. To understand this important decision, let's first look at a chart, then the earnings backdrop and, finally, the decision.
Chart
Please click here (https://thearorareport.com/chart-stock-market-average-true-range) for the annotated chart. The chart is of S&P 500 ETF (SPY). Similar observations can be made from the charts of Dow Jones Industrial Average , Nasdaq 100 ETF (QQQ) and small-cap ETF (IWM). For transparency, this is exactly the same chart that was previously published.
Please observe the following from the chart:
-- The chart shows, with red rectangles, the times when the daily range expanded.
-- The chart also shows that when the daily range expanded, there was usually a dip in the market.
-- The chart shows that most of the dips have been less than 20%, but the market was cut nearly in half during 2008 range expansion.
Here is the most important question from the chart: "How big will the ultimate drop be from the current range expansion, or has the maximum drop already happened?"

Earnings backdrop
In the very long term, the big determinate of stock prices is earnings. When Dow Jones Industrial Average was trading around 18,000 points and almost nobody was talking about the kind of bullish market we have seen, The Arora Report laid out a case for Dow 30,000 and subsequently repeated it. Please see "Here's the case for Dow 30,000 in Trump's first term (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/heres-the-case-for-dow-30000-in-trumps-first-term-2017-02-17)."
Technical backdrop
As The Arora Report has previously shown, from a technical perspective, higher prices are still likely ahead, though with more volatility. Please click here (https://thearorareport.com/chart-stock-market-consolidation-es-02222018) for a chart showing the bullish "W" pattern. For details, please see "Charts show that Dow 30,000 is still likely (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/charts-show-that-dow-30000-is-still-likely-2018-02-23)."
For a longer-term perspective, please click here (https://thearorareport.com/chart-dow-jones-industrial-average-stock-market-technical-analysis-01052018) to see this chart for a measured target of the stock market. For the sake of transparency, these are exactly the same charts that were previously published.
The decision
If a trade war breaks out, the projected earnings that were the basis of the case for Dow 30,000, published by The Arora Report when Dow was around 18,000, will likely not come true.
It is difficult to rely on statements from President Trump because his rhetoric often changes and sometimes does not match his actions. He has said he will levy a 25% tariff on imported steel and 10% on aluminum.
How do investors get an early indication of which way a potential trade war is going to go? Investors should look for a decision by Trump to name the replacement for Gary Cohn, the economic adviser who resigned this week amid the announcement of the tariffs. If Trump replaces Cohn, a free-market thinker, with a pragmatic person, it would be positive for stock markets around the world. On the other hand, if the replacement is an ideological hard-liner, it would be a big negative for the markets.
Right now investors don't believe there will be a trade war. This is evident from the price performance of popular stocks such as Apple (AAPL), Boeing (BA) and Microsoft (MSFT).
